independent_acceptance.source_scope: Theorem 2 says any permutation group; introductory N_n definition permits reducible polynomials and F_n explicitly counts fields. No preceding global n>=5 or transitivity restriction was found in the checked introduction.
independent_acceptance.independent_reason: The C2 action on three letters is intransitive, whereas embeddings of a cubic field form one orbit. Thus F3=0 allows a=1/8. For H divisible by four, H+1 even b and H/4 positive c=2 mod4 yield H(H+1)/4 distinct Eisenstein quadratic times x examples, with distinct roots and exact C2 action. The ratio to H^(3/2)log(H)^2 diverges.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_repair: Theorem 7 separately handles intransitive groups but does not limit Theorem 2. Restricting Theorem 2 to transitive groups removes this counterexample; replacing fields by etale algebras requires new hypotheses. Theorem 1 is not refuted.

independent_acceptance.source_scope: Corollary 8 allows k=9 and G=S9; the paper explicitly uses subset notation including equality in its Theorem 2 discussion.
independent_acceptance.independent_reason: Independently factored the exact reported coefficient polynomial using installed SymPy modulo13,17,19: squarefree degree patterns (9),(1,8),(1,1,1,1,1,1,1,2). The 9-cycle gives transitivity; an 8-cycle stabilizer is transitive on the remaining points, hence the group is 2-transitive; conjugate transpositions generate S9. CRT fixes one positive-density class of nine coefficients. A fixed M11 Galois extension exists from the regular realizations recalled in the preserved primary Section2 plus Hilbert irreducibility; the faithful 11-point action supplies an index11 fixed field and hence the required monic integral degree11 polynomial. Simplicity and the prime11 divisor rule out a nontrivial common quotient with S9, so product Galois group and injective bounded-height multiplication follow.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_repair: The lower bound H^9 contradicts exponent8.686 only in the stated product scope. Replaced the unverified exact Lemma2 locator by the actually retained Section2 basis and supplied the fixed-field argument. Isolated M11 bound is unaffected.

issues.title: Theorem 7 proof derives exact-height bounds from cumulative bounds
issues.complete_verification: Sparse masses m(2^j)=2^(2j) have cumulative O(T^2) but unbounded m(T)/T.
issues.counterevidence: Not asserted to be polynomial counts; a dyadic proof recovers the applications for alpha>0,beta>=0.
issues.core_impact: Invalid indispensable inference in a principal theorem and application.
issues.repair: Use dyadic convolution with Mahler-height constants; state parameter restrictions.

independent_acceptance.source_scope: Theorem7 hypotheses are cumulative counts; source line1153 inserts an exact-height bound with exponent alpha1-1.
independent_acceptance.independent_reason: For m(2^j)=4^j, the geometric sum is at most(4/3)T^2 while m(2^j)/(2^j) diverges, disproving the stated logical implication. It is explicitly not an actual polynomial sequence. With H*=max(1,coefficient height), Mahler comparison gives bounded product heights; dyadic cumulative counting with positive largest exponent and nonnegative logarithmic exponents yields exactly the report composition exponent and handles factors of smaller exponent geometrically.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_repair: The applications survive the supplied dyadic repair. This does not justify negative-logarithm ranges or F03 exponent8.686, and it does not assert Theorem7 false.
